title: Falcon Space Biefeld-Brown vacuum test: rotation reverses as pressure drops

tellings.quote:
they did the tests at not too low
pressure and they noticed it spinning in
one direction and then eventually they
kept pumping down further and further
and eventually it started spinning in
the other direction which

plain: A device meant to show the Biefeld-Brown effect, a claimed push produced by high-voltage electric charge, was tested in a vacuum chamber at a company called Falcon Space. It is said to have spun one way at moderately low pressure, then spun the opposite way as the air was pumped out further. David Chester, a theoretical physicist and a friend of Michels, tells this on the show while testing claims of electrostatic thrust made by Charles Buhler, an engineer the episode connects to NASA. He passes on the result without naming a source, and mentions the space-propulsion writer Tim Ventura and a man called Mark. It matters because whether the push survives with no air around is the test of whether it is anything more than moving air.
